doc.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Depression years on the family cotton farm
summary: The Depression barely registered; the family raised its own food, cotton, corn and onions.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I had a question, I was wondering about the depression years for your family. Did it affect your lifestyle and the economy of the area you were in?

It certainly did but I didn’t notice it too much because I mean I was just, that’s the way things were. And we always had great food, well we raised a lot of it ourselves. And I had very loving parents. I was very fortunate, and a sister and a brother.
Did your parents stay on that farm for their whole life?
And it was mostly a cotton farm was it?
Well yeah, principally. And we raised corn to feed the animals you know, and onions we raised onions.
